characters.description: A spear fighter, maker, and Earth heretic whose soul world is the Alpha Cosmos. He opens the book by challenging the settlement to prove that its collective strength can withstand the greater calamities he expects the system to bring.
characters.name: Randidly Ghosthound

characters.description: An off-world spear fighter who wishes to serve as Randidly's knight. Earth's restrictions sharply suppress her abilities, so she enters a dangerous dungeon and subjects herself to an extreme training schedule.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A young woman who leads the sprigget settlement research effort. She agrees to design Randidly's articulated replacement arm, charging him a class lighthouse he does not need and a favor to be collected later.
characters.name: The sprigget head engineer

characters.description: A settlement craftsman who supplies Randidly with a darksteel armor set and continues developing equipment for him.
characters.name: The settlement smith

characters.description: The spirit of a settlement who knows about the system's architecture. Concealed ether machinery around her oak blocks the system overlay and hides itself from system observation.
characters.name: The village spirit

characters.description: Randidly's soulbound ally and a covert defender of Earth. When his missing riders fail to return, he suspects that she has redirected them to a mission of her own beyond the sea, where her larger purpose is still unclear.
characters.name: Nevaeh

characters.description: Randidly's autonomous weapon and ally. Its growing aggression resembles Thorn's behavior, and it demonstrates extreme combat power by destroying a settlement built around a tier-two raid boss.
characters.name: Acri

characters.description: Randidly's first soul seed, whose underground body extends beneath much of Scant. Thorn is substantially stronger than Acri and Sulphur when it reunites with them and Randidly.
characters.name: Thorn

characters.description: A settlement craftsman determined to surpass three level-79 weapons sent by Zone 7. He resolves to answer the unsolicited gift with superior work and advance as the Dawnsmith.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: A village spirit with privileged knowledge of the system's framework. She asks whether Randidly can grant her a class, offers intelligence in exchange for an honest answer, and warns that a powerful outside actor has complicated his approaching judgment.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: A settlement contact asked by a Zone 7 delegation to connect the capital transport networks of the two zones.
characters.name: Donnie

characters.description: A feared pirate and former ally of Randidly. Known publicly as the Pale Killer, he boards Randidly's hired ship and is emotionally shattered when Randidly recognizes the hardship behind his violent reputation.
characters.name: Declan

characters.description: An undying skeletal instigator who fled through the portal to the frog world. He has encouraged powerful local factions to invade Earth, making his capture necessary before a peaceful solution can be attempted.
characters.name: Roy

characters.description: A frog-person academy graduate who volunteers to guide the Demon Prince south in place of a spawnmate. Though wary of Randidly, he is capable, locally knowledgeable, and unaffiliated with a Toad Lord.
characters.name: Shual

characters.description: A settlement civic leader who directs the immediate diplomatic response to Zone 7.
characters.name: Mrs. Hamilton

characters.description: Sam's partner, who is developing coffee for trade.
characters.name: Regina

characters.description: A giant flaming skeletal bear allied with the force raiding the settlement. It arrives through an enemy transfer, destroys one of Regina's spirit allies, and adds overwhelming physical force to the attackers' coordinated assault.
characters.name: Chrysanthemum

characters.description: A settlement spear fighter who blocks Thea near the Zone 7 teleporter.
characters.name: Alana

characters.description: An attacker whom Alana blocks near the settlement's Zone 7 teleporter during the raid.
characters.name: Thea

characters.description: Sidney's altered lieutenant, found with Roy after maroon crystal has blinded or otherwise blocked his senses. Unable to distinguish ally from enemy, he attacks indiscriminately while bearing an unknown destructive power.
characters.name: Drake

characters.description: Nathan's sibling and a person known to have a connection with Randidly. A hostile group selects her as its captive during a coordinated raid.
characters.name: Kirstie

characters.description: Randidly's adviser within the Alpha Cosmos. She treats the rescued Kirstie and helps him study a disintegrating system construct that turns the force of images into simpler statistical power, offering both technical and political counsel.
characters.name: Lucretia

characters.description: A settlement spellcaster who reports on Zone 11, traces portal energy eastward, and uses a cloud-steed skill for rapid travel.
characters.name: Clarissa

characters.description: An established resident and political negotiator within the Alpha Cosmos. Randidly entrusts him with cautious contact after mist recedes to reveal an unfamiliar populated continent, relying on him to limit the risk of immediate conflict.
characters.name: The Monster Prince

characters.description: A rapidly developing fighter in squad 25 who specializes in awareness and defense. She enters the settlement's challenge alongside her sibling, Pan Cortez.
characters.name: Isabella Cortez

characters.description: A rapidly developing fighter in squad 25 whose attacks reduce an opponent's stamina. He enters the settlement's challenge alongside his sibling, Isabella Cortez.
characters.name: Pan Cortez

characters.description: The level-57 captain of the settlement's 10th Squad. Acting on Stan's order, he attempts a concealed attack on Randidly before the next challenge rung begins.
characters.name: Eli Iron

characters.description: The settlement's elected military commander. Strategically capable but deeply afraid of Randidly, he authorizes a surprise attack between challenge rounds in hopes of breaking the appearance of invulnerability.
characters.name: Stan

characters.description: A settlement fighter assigned with Alana and the Cortez siblings to contain Helen during the decisive challenge battle.
characters.name: Dozer

characters.description: The settlement civic leader previously known as Mrs. Hamilton, whose name is revealed when Randidly addresses her as Miranda before the decisive challenge fight.
characters.name: Miranda

characters.description: A barrier-and-array user whom Miranda is preparing as a possible future leader. The settlement's dwindling force relies on him to complete a prepared control skill while the other fighters occupy Randidly.
characters.name: Beryl

characters.description: Randidly's contact for mobilizing the Order Dukies. Randidly identifies him as the person who can bring the order's forces south as new threats demand attention.
characters.name: Naffer

characters.description: An Erickson Steel receptionist with the Meticulous Technician class and an exceptional preparation skill. Her careful judgment leads her to trust Randidly's identity and escort him to the company's acting leadership.
characters.name: Vi

characters.description: One of Erickson Steel's managers during a coordinated financial and regulatory campaign against the company. She explains how targeted taxes and proposed inspections threaten its independence.
characters.name: Tatiana

characters.description: A financial and political opponent of Erickson Steel who wants control of the company and its metal technology. He works with Senator Heathridge, providing funds and operational support while their pressure campaign begins to lose leverage.
characters.name: Evan Crane

characters.description: A political sponsor of the campaign against Erickson Steel. He directs Evan Crane to fund their final plan and wait for instructions as the company's rail technology attracts a powerful institutional ally.
characters.name: Senator Heathridge

characters.description: Leader of one of Randidly's increasingly independent rider factions. Randidly formally names him and his group the Legion of the Unbreakable Bulwark after they bring back mutated dungeon monsters and request identities for their competing forces.
characters.name: Kingsley

characters.description: Leader of a rival faction among Randidly's summoned riders. Randidly names his silk-camp group the Legion of the Unavoidable Pivots as the riders develop stronger organization and distinct identities.
characters.name: Trap

characters.description: The knight-errant of Randidly's order, earlier introduced as Naffer. At the Orchard lottery, he represents the order and asks candidates to show the ideals and commitment behind their intended futures.
characters.name: Naffer Sweet

characters.description: The Orchard lottery organizer who chooses Vi as his opponent after identifying her as one of the few contestants without a combat class.
characters.name: Roland

characters.description: Leader of the organized monster resistance inside the dungeon. After her people devise traps that kill several riders, she receives Randidly when he enters their hidden cave complex to demand surrender.
characters.name: The bird-monster war priestess

characters.description: An Alpha Cosmos artificer and moving-city designer who works from a private workshop. Randidly approaches her to discuss possible internships at her company and asks her to undertake the design of a giant mobile city.
characters.name: Wendy

characters.description: An Alpha Cosmos fighter with the Morningstar Vanguard class. She tells Randidly that she has moved beyond obsessive training, pursued ordinary experiences, and found a more independent form of growth.
characters.name: Azrael

characters.description: The prince and heir of the Armgrast Empire, initially presented as the diamond merchant Lazar Stone. Randidly recognizes both his identity and his connection to the formation anchoring the Alpha Cosmos.
characters.name: Lazarus

characters.description: A dying fourth-cohort artist-warrior awakened from a crystal coffin beneath the dungeon. Nether corruption consumes him, while the enduring image in his artwork is revealed as the source of the dungeon's timeless atmosphere.
characters.name: The entombed monkey warrior

recaps.ending: After eleven dungeon months, Randidly can embody his images more reliably and has developed practical large-scale engraving, but his artificial left arm is destroyed and his class remains structurally damaged. Wendy receives the moving-city project, the rescued mollusks, and dungeon resources. Randidly spares Prince Lazarus after defeating him, leaving Azrael to treat the anchor-linked prince while the Alpha Cosmos approaches a possible war without Randidly's direct intervention. On Earth, Helen remains his active ally, Naffer is building an Order Dukies training program at Erickson Steel, and Vi joins it with a painful, persistent Reject effect in her left hand. Nevaeh still contains the frog-world threat through fear, while Roy and Drake remain captive. Beneath the dungeon plateau, a terminally Nether-corrupted warrior gives Randidly a Nether bomb and an empowered chisel-glove. He explains that the system uses worlds as recruits in a war against oblivion and that Randidly's heretic judgment will probably require surviving limited front-line service. Randidly's Touch from Beyond reveals its mythic form as Nether's Caress, a power that risks corruption and severe injury. He promises not to refuse a future chance to strike the system, though the warrior's account and the exact terms of the judgment remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Randidly challenges the settlement to confront its dependence on him, then interrupts his preparations to contain a frog-world invasion and rescue Kirstie from raiders. Back home, he and Helen fight the settlement through an escalating public ladder that ends in a catastrophic draw and leaves both the community and Randidly changed. He protects Erickson Steel from political pressure, teaches image-based forging, and enters a time-dilated dungeon to prepare for his heretic judgment. Eleven months of training yield stronger images and large-scale living engravings, but cost him his artificial arm and involve the destruction of an organized monster people. In the Alpha Cosmos, he refuses to dictate a looming war and spares the anchor-linked Prince Lazarus. Beneath the dungeon plateau, a dying fourth-cohort warrior reveals that the system recruits worlds for a war against oblivion, gives Randidly a Nether bomb and empowered glove, and indicates that his judgment will demand front-line survival. Randidly leaves with a dangerous Nether skill, a damaged class, and no settled answer to the wider conflict.

recaps.text: Previously: Randidly Ghosthound became one of Earth's leading fighters while resisting the system's attempts to define and control his growth. His power increasingly depends on images, especially Yggdrasil, and on the Alpha Cosmos within his soul. He leads an order, owns Erickson Steel, and carries responsibility for allies on Earth and lives inside his soul world. His disputes with the system have marked him as a heretic and placed a judgment in his future. Helen, an off-world spear fighter, seeks to stand beside him as his knight. Nevaeh remains bound to him and operates independently in defense of Earth. Lyra possesses knowledge of system architecture but has repeatedly proven difficult to trust. Earth is still connecting zones and approaching further calamities, while hostile forces, political rivalries, and portals to other worlds keep its position unstable. Randidly begins this volume convinced that humanity's present security is misleading and that dependence on a few exceptional fighters will not survive what comes next.

Randidly argues that the settlement's collective image is brittle and accepts a nine-stage challenge against its organized forces. He intends the contest to expose complacency before future calamities arrive. Helen asks to fight beside him, but Earth's restrictions suppress her strength, so she begins severe dungeon training instead. Randidly also needs a functional left arm. A sprigget engineer supplies a mechanical design, a settlement smith helps forge the pieces from an improved blood-steel alloy, and Randidly engraves the arm with a powerful imbalance-exploiting strike. He rejects darksteel armor because it suppresses the image-based growth he considers essential. Meanwhile, the village spirit shows him a concealed floating-island ark intended to evacuate Earth if survival becomes impossible. Several summoned riders fail to return, creating another urgent problem. With the arm completed and tested against a high-level bear, Randidly heads southeast to recover them before the public challenge begins.

Randidly reaches the harbor settlement of Scant and learns that Nevaeh has been using his riders in a hidden campaign across the sea. On the journey, Lyra asks him for a class and warns that a stronger power has interfered with his coming judgment. The feared pirate called the Pale Killer proves to be Declan, a former ally broken by Tara's death and the failed attempts to revive her. Declan leads Randidly through a portal into a frog-person world. There, Nevaeh poses as a Great Demon King and destroys local rulers to conceal Earth's weakness from a much stronger invasion force. The undying skeleton Roy has encouraged distant Toad Lords to attack Earth, so Randidly adopts the role of Demon Prince and pursues him south with Shual, a frog-person academy graduate who volunteered as guide. Along the way, Randidly spares an intelligent level-70 boar whose maroon skeletal arm appears to act against it. Roy, the portal threat, and the origin of the frog world's imposed ether supply remain unresolved.

Randidly enters a deep frog city while following Roy's trail. Its Toad Lord demonstrates control over subordinates' ether, confirms that a skeletal emissary promoted an invasion of Earth, and tries to poison Randidly. Randidly kills him but still cannot identify the source of the world's feed system. At the same time, Thea's group launches a coordinated raid on the settlement. Regina, Mrs. Hamilton, Alana, and other defenders drive back attackers that include the flaming skeletal bear Chrysanthemum and a winged portal-maker. Randidly catches Roy and discovers Drake beside him, blinded and driven indiscriminately violent by a maroon-crystal Fate. A portal lets the raiders retrieve them. Thea reveals that an unknown patron demanded someone connected to Randidly in exchange for settling Chrysanthemum's revival debt, and her group abducts Kirstie. Randidly forces his way through their portal, transfers Kirstie to safety, and overwhelms several attackers. Thea, Drake, and surviving allies escape after Chrysanthemum absorbs heavy damage and the portal array is destroyed. Kirstie is rescued, but Randidly cannot pursue immediately.

Back in the Alpha Cosmos, Randidly and Lucretia study a system construct that reduces image power to simpler statistical output. The discovery strengthens his belief that images can exceed the system's intended limits. Helen completes a dream trial, reaches level 50 with a Fate, and earns a place beside him in the settlement challenge. Randidly experiments with merging his Ash and Spear Phantom styles, develops a mana-engraving image within Yggdrasil, and tests four powerful items made by Sam. The items carry histories Sam did not consciously invent, raising concern that earlier blessings have connected Randidly to an unknown influence. Mist also clears inside the Alpha Cosmos, revealing a populated continent whose history matches those item legends. Randidly orders cautious contact through the Monster Prince. With little time left, he decides to form the Ashen Phantom under the pressure of live combat. The public challenge begins with Randidly and Helen facing the settlement's lower-ranked squads before a divided crowd.

Randidly's Ashen Phantom overwhelms the first two hundred fighters, while Helen defeats the next rung through her blood-sea image. Together and separately, they continue through veteran squads. The Cortez siblings briefly test Randidly through coordinated defense and stamina drain, but he defeats them and directs them toward future training. The contest changes when military commander Stan authorizes Eli Iron to strike Randidly between rounds. The ambush fails with catastrophic injuries to Eli, and Randidly enters the next battle knowing the settlement has tried to manipulate him. He releases Yggdrasil and nearly turns its judgment on Stan. His accumulated images demand a death he is unwilling to deliver, creating a crisis that threatens their stability. Contact with the Monster Prince's independent pursuit of peace gives Randidly another answer: the settlement must carry responsibility for its own path. He rewrites Yggdrasil's judgment, evolves a powerful root skill, and forces the elite squad toward surrender without executing Stan.

Mrs. Hamilton interrogates Stan and confirms that the surprise attack was designed to cloud Randidly's judgment and exploit his instinct to protect the settlement. Randidly concludes that shielding the community from consequences will only preserve its weakness. Clarissa then challenges him with increasingly destructive weather magic, but Yggdrasil eventually collapses her wind entity. Two elite squads enter next. Their leaders nearly sever Randidly's mechanical arm and expose the poor transition between his separate spear styles. Under their pressure, Randidly forcibly merges the styles into the mythic Descent of the Grim Chimera. The system recognizes him as Earth's first mythic-rarity individual, awards the First Key to the Nexus, and opens a possible route for territory or the world to ascend with additional keys. The violent Chimera image transforms his combat and lets him defeat both elite leaders. The new finishing technique is decisive, but its effects and bodily cost remain unknown as the settlement prepares its combined final force.

Randidly learns that his mythic finishing move draws on unrealized paths through time and can inflict lasting damage when the chosen variation is too distant. The settlement gathers fifty-two fighters for a decisive combined battle, planning to separate Helen, suppress Randidly's plants, and use their Fates to resist his images. Randidly answers with Yggdrasil, the Grim Chimera, roots, and summoned riders. Alana drives Helen away while Miranda, Sam, Clarissa, Donnie, and the rest coordinate frost, barriers, curses, summons, and close attacks against Randidly. Declan emerges from concealment to wound him but is defeated. The defenders suffer mounting injuries as Randidly breaks their formations and interrupts Clarissa's major wind ritual. Their last tactic requires sacrifices: Donnie returns damage dealt to Paolo, Sam ruins his frost hammer, and Rayna briefly commands Randidly to remain still. Those moments let Beryl complete Isolate. Randidly loses every ordinary sense, yet remains physically unharmed and able to reach his inner world. Through the Grim Chimera, he detects Alana approaching.

While Randidly remains trapped in sensory isolation, Helen fights Dozer alone. Her declaration that she is Randidly's knight briefly loosens Earth's restrictions, allowing her to defeat Dozer despite a broken femur. Alana sends the remaining leaders away and confronts Randidly with an emerging Valkyrie image sustained partly by the settlement's gathered belief. Randidly manifests the Grim Chimera directly through his body, and their exchanges destroy the arena. The final collision opens a much larger collapse that consumes the quarry, lightly damages the production district, and leaves a dangerous sinkhole under the settlement. Both Alana and Randidly survive. Alana begins practicing a smaller orange image that belongs more fully to her, while Randidly recovers in isolation and Helen serves as his contact with the leadership. The settlement awards Randidly the completed rung, but the arena's destruction postpones the last stage indefinitely. Publicly, the challenge ends as an indefinite draw.

A delegation from Zone 11 asks the settlement for help against weekly waves of level-70 monsters. In the frog world, Roy and Drake remain prisoners of a powerful ruler, with Drake tortured and Roy threatened for refusing to yield. Randidly withdraws after the challenge, stabilizes the conflict between his images, and turns to Erickson Steel as his heretic judgment approaches. He gains major path rewards, gives the settlement energy-rich fruits, and postpones Lyra's request for a class because it could give her dangerous influence. At Erickson Steel, Tatiana explains that hostile interests are using taxes, debt, and proposed regulation to seize control. Randidly consolidates operations, asks Naffer to establish an Order Dukies base, and begins improving rail cars and materials. Vi's careful judgment earns Tatiana's trust. Randidly then completes Perfect Soulbond with Nevaeh. His awareness reaches an immense engraved crystal barrier, where a hostile presence attacks through his soul space and partially shatters his class before following a karmic connection toward an unidentified creature. His soul skill begins repairs, but the threat is unidentified.

Nevaeh uses their new doppelganger connection to examine Randidly and finds traces of the hostile being's rigid ether. Randidly clears them through sustained ether output and restores balance between Yggdrasil and the Grim Chimera, reducing the pain from his damaged class. He publicly teaches Erickson Steel's smelters to forge through images. Their first attempts already surpass the company's previous alloys, and his own samples exceed them by a wide margin. Inspired by the demonstration, Vi resigns to seek an independent path with Tatiana's support. Senator Heathridge and Evan Crane continue attacks on the company through staged government demands and a hired infiltrator, but Helen kills the saboteur before he can act. Alana prepares a settlement force to aid Zone 11 while struggling to form an image without the conditions of her duel. Randidly confirms that dungeon time pauses his judgment timer, harvests hundreds of stone golems, and gains new control and willpower insights. He heads west to find a higher-level dungeon suitable for extended preparation.

Political pressure on Erickson Steel escalates when Helen kills another suspected agent, admits it, and incapacitates officers who attempt to detain her. Randidly enters a level-67 time-dilated dungeon where one outside month could contain years. He builds a forge and training base beside a timeless monolith and discovers arrows pointing toward a forbidden plateau. Closer examination shows that his class only appears repaired: later levels no longer strengthen its underlying image, so he commits to a year of refinement. His ether awakens a community of clockwork-building mollusks and encourages his summoned riders to form competing factions led by Kingsley and Trap. Outside, Vi accepts an Orchard lottery certificate and seeks a place in the Order Dukies. Naffer asks candidates to demonstrate the ideals behind their desired futures. Vi reaches the final duel against Roland, an experienced light user with a condensed Fate. Her prepared rituals break his defenses, but he escalates to lethal attacks. With her charms exhausted and an ion bolt closing, she must rely on her bare hands and pen.

Vi disperses Roland's ion bolt with an improvised hand technique but loses the duel and is badly injured. Naffer stops further violence and accepts responsibility. Randidly refuses to impose peace on the Alpha Cosmos when Lucretia reports that a neighboring nation is militarizing, recognizing its inhabitants as separate lives despite their bond to him. Heathridge's legal campaign against Erickson Steel fails, though he misreads the company's activity as a covert political coalition. In the dungeon, Randidly's riders add a third legion, then face an organized monster resistance led by a bird-monster war priestess. She refuses surrender or flight, and the three legions eradicate her people. Randidly later counts 9,106 dead and admits that his haste and suspicion made the outcome a mistake. Vi wakes with a damaged left hand bearing the persistent Reject effect and joins the Order Dukies training camp at Erickson Steel. After eight dungeon months, Randidly succeeds in creating a huge levelable engraving through repeated use of his mythic time-variation skill. The five-day experiment destroys his base dome and artificial left arm, but establishes that large scale can make image distribution manageable.

The mollusk settlement develops internal conflict over automatons, so Randidly offers its people a new purpose outside the dungeon. He asks Wendy to design a moving city and later entrusts her with the mollusks and gathered resources. In the Alpha Cosmos, Azrael explains that she has found growth beyond obsessive training. Her host, Lazar Stone, is exposed as Prince Lazarus and as one of the people anchoring the Alpha Cosmos. Lazarus claims that the connection could let him seize the world, then attacks. Randidly defeats him but spares his life, leaving Azrael to treat him while the threat remains open. After eleven months of training, Randidly follows the ancient arrows onto the forbidden plateau. His three rider legions engage the gathered monster refugees while he enters a vast crater alone. A trail of engraved beacons leads past a damaged mythic chisel-glove, immense bone piles, and a lake of liquefied ether. At the bottom, Randidly finds a decaying crystal coffin whose surviving instructions tell him to break it. Concluding that the entire path was deliberately prepared, he uses the glove to strike the coffin.

The coffin releases a red-haired monkey warrior dying from a Nether wound. His enduring artwork created the dungeon's timeless image, and he learns that his former fourth-cohort world has been reduced to a system dungeon. He explains that his world survived three calamities, then received a fourth requiring a century of front-line service in the Great War. Nether-distorted time made his years count as only days, causing failure and leaving his world abandoned. He believes the system recruits worlds for a war against oblivion, converts unstable level-50 Fates into weapons, and discards worlds that cannot meet its demands. The warrior gives Randidly a contained Nether bomb and returns the chisel-glove empowered by his remaining timelessness. He says Randidly's heretic judgment will probably require proving his value through a limited term on those same front lines, though the duration is unknown. When Randidly activates Touch from Beyond, he discovers its mythic form, Nether's Caress, which manifests Nether at the cost of corruption and severe bodily harm. Randidly promises not to refuse a future opportunity to strike the system. He leaves the encounter stronger in knowledge and dangerous tools, but without a left arm, a repaired class, or certainty about the wider war.

characters.description: The founder of the mobile-city project, working with Wendy to forge a mechanical replacement for his missing left arm. His command of rare materials lets him undertake construction that other engineers cannot safely perform.
characters.name: Randidly Ghosthound

characters.description: The chief engineer behind Randidly's mechanical city. She directs its design work but depends on him to shape materials beyond her level and technical reach.
characters.name: Wendy

characters.name: Lucretia

characters.description: A spear fighter who joins the expedition investigating reports of a dragon on Mount Olympus.
characters.name: Alana

characters.description: The archer in the Mount Olympus expedition investigating a reported dragon.
characters.name: Annie

characters.description: The leader of Zone 11 and a member of the Mount Olympus expedition investigating a reported dragon.
characters.name: Warlord

characters.name: Ice Dragon Broodmother

characters.description: The administrator of Randidly's company. She recognizes that a government land proposal is designed to gain leverage over the organization and handles the negotiation with caution.
characters.name: Tatiana

characters.description: A formidable ally of Randidly who is available to defend the company from the monsters gathering nearby, though she longs for more demanding opponents.
characters.name: Helen

characters.name: Senator Heathridge

characters.description: An operative aligned with Senator Heathridge who tries to use a rival engineering order and a nearby monster threat to pressure Randidly's company.
characters.name: Evan Crane

characters.description: The leader of Randidly's training order. Having endured Randidly's demanding personal instruction, he now oversees an equally severe program for new aspirants.
characters.name: Naffer

characters.description: An aspirant in Randidly's training order who persists through raids, weighted movement, and repeated duels. Her determination is tested by the program's escalating demands.
characters.name: Vi

characters.description: A training-order applicant who works beside Vi during the order's demanding program.
characters.name: Garrett

characters.description: A woman who arranged Randidly's earlier dungeon encounter and bargains to provide information about the System in exchange for a class.
characters.name: The woman seeking a class

characters.description: The Order Dukies aspirant previously introduced as Vi, now identified by her full name. She formerly worked around Randidly's company as an assistant to Tatiana.
characters.name: Vi Riverson

characters.description: The Order Dukies applicant previously introduced as Garrett, now identified by his full name. He assists Vi during the company festival.
characters.name: Garrett Tysven

characters.description: Randidly's developing fire image, which begins changing while he forges and engraves a difficult promised vessel.
characters.name: Ignition Essence

characters.description: A composite biological intelligence formed from six brains and able to work through mechanical drones. It warns Randidly of several emerging dangers and requests an open future favor in return for helping his city project.
characters.name: Ghost

characters.description: Randidly's father, reported to have left a trail of deaths after separating from Hank Howard. His purpose and present destination are unclear.
characters.name: Ezekiel Ghosthound

characters.description: An unidentified killer moving south whose dead victims have been drained of blood and whose survivors are left mentally broken.
characters.name: Stroud

characters.description: A specialist who arrives with a companion to address the damage to Randidly's class.
characters.name: Nathan

characters.description: Randidly's world-tree image and one of the animi used in Nathan's effort to stabilize his damaged class.
characters.name: Yggdrasil

characters.description: A village spirit who is also a human individual seeking greater autonomy. She brings Randidly information about Shawl's failed Nexus test and the accelerated calamity facing his world, while trying to regain Randidly's trust.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: The financially strained Zone 1 power broker previously known as Senator Heathridge. He seeks control of Randidly's company and equips Evan Crane with an experimental exosuit.
characters.name: Senator Cliff Heathridge

characters.description: A companion bound to Randidly who is investigating the dangerous toad world and developing greater control over raw ether. She confronts and comforts him before they spar ahead of his departure.
characters.name: Nevaeh

characters.description: A hostile investigator who enters Karen’s reactor with Evan Crane and Senator Cliff Heathridge. The group accuses Randidly of using imports that violate Zone 7 law.
characters.name: Chuck Ballard

characters.description: The developing spirit of Randidly's mobile city, able to decide independently when and where the city moves.
characters.name: Karen

characters.description: A dragon-headed liaison who introduces Randidly and his separated images to the Nether warfront, explains its hazards, and links his own advancement to their performance.
characters.name: Zagnall

characters.description: The manifested form of Randidly's fire image, previously known as Ignition Essence. It arrives at the Nether warfront alongside the Grim Chimera and Yggdrasil.
characters.name: Ignition of the Emerald Essence

characters.name: Lord Milne

characters.name: The feathered commander

characters.description: The feathered commander's lieutenant, who escorts Randidly from her tent to the staging area for his Great Rift mission.
characters.name: The granite-bodied lieutenant

characters.description: A gauntleted front-line fighter with turquoise hair who briefly approaches Randidly during his training, then withdraws with her two companions before explaining her purpose.
characters.name: The turquoise-haired soldier

characters.description: A silent, rock-bodied woman assigned to serve under Randidly at the front. He suspects she may also be observing him for someone else.
characters.name: The rock-bodied subordinate

characters.description: An anxious, snake-headed fighter assigned to Randidly's front-line group. He carries two small scimitars.
characters.name: The snake-headed subordinate

characters.description: The warfront authority who retains custody of Randidly’s imprisoned physical body while his conscious image serves in the fighting.
characters.name: The supreme commander

characters.description: An unnamed old woman who shares control of the fate armory and possesses image mastery beyond the nearby commanders.
characters.name: The fate-armory elder

characters.description: An elder who guards the fate armory and leads Randidly to the dormant sword blade once carried by her dead daughter. She warns that accepting it could consume him.
characters.name: Nadia

characters.description: A member of Randidly's strategic-key party who remains with the group after its dangerous visit to the fate armory.
characters.name: Salazar

characters.description: A borderlands refugee recently brought to Karen and Tatiana's former partner from before the System. She has an affinity with moss spirits and openly questions Randidly's leadership and absence.
characters.name: Felicia

characters.description: Ezekiel's helmeted combat companion, who fights under the persona Dauntless. He uses a sea-and-ship image against the blood beasts surrounding a healer's cabin.
characters.name: Ace

characters.description: Zone 19’s leading healer. She resists an abduction attempt by Ezekiel and Ace and can use holy power to eradicate blood beasts, although repeated use leaves her exhausted.
characters.name: The red-haired healer

characters.description: A maker who completes a seven-dawn forging ritual to produce a massive shield for Earth's defense against a possible Ogre invasion.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: The first chairwoman elected by the World Summit. Her one-year term places her at the head of the emerging coalition among Earth's zones.
characters.name: Theodora Grayman

characters.description: A commander who has recaptured the escaped Nether Prince.
characters.name: Commander Tarith

recaps.ending: Randidly escapes the strategic-key deployment by using Nether's Caress to move his physical body through the Great Rift. He reunites with the Grim Chimera and Yggdrasil, combining his ether crossroads with five Nether cores and regaining Tier I citizen rights. Disguised as a Nether Beast, he reaches the collapsing front and saves the badly wounded turquoise-haired soldier. Absolute Grasp of Yggdrasil destroys most of a ten-thousand-beast formation, allowing the feathered commander and her lieutenant to engage the surviving elites. The battle remains active, with Gatekeeper-level enemies still dangerous. Ignition Essence is missing after its containment begins to fail. On Earth, Karen continues under Tatiana, Alana has opened uncertain talks with the dragons, and Theodora Grayman chairs the new World Summit. Ezekiel escapes Stroud with Ace and a healer, while the Ogre Gorge and Rakshasi threats remain unresolved. Randidly and the turquoise-haired soldier acknowledge mutual feelings, but he keeps his distance because her ancient, familiar ether may be dangerous.
recaps.in_short: Randidly completes his replacement arm and launches Karen, an autonomous moving city, before his heretic judgment conscripts him into the Nether war. His body is imprisoned while his conscious Grim Chimera image fights beside Yggdrasil and the damaged Ignition Essence. He survives lethal missions, learns to manipulate Nether, helps the turquoise-haired soldier destroy a Netherwell base, acquires a volatile blade Fate and a sealed trunk, and condenses true Nether cores during a strategic-key exile. Earth continues without him as Tatiana runs Karen, Vi supports his training order, and Alana turns her dragon hunt into possible diplomacy. A Nether King's invasion finally gives Randidly the opening to recover his body through the Great Rift. Reunited with the Grim Chimera and Yggdrasil, he destroys most of a vast lesser force and saves the wounded soldier, but elite enemies remain, the front-line command conflict is unsettled, and Ignition Essence has not returned.

recaps.text: Previously: Randidly Ghosthound became one of Earth's foremost fighters and image-makers while building an organization able to endure the System's escalating threats. His power brought obligations beyond Earth, damage to his class, and an approaching judgment for heresy. He also lost his left arm. As the new volume begins, he is preparing for a long absence while his company, allies, and manifested images carry responsibilities he cannot manage alone.

Randidly works with Wendy and Lucretia to complete a mechanical left arm and advance plans for a moving city. Elsewhere, Alana's Mount Olympus expedition finds not one dragon but an Ice Dragon Broodmother and its young. Alana survives being frozen and thrown from the mountain, gains new abilities, and realizes that trying to embody her whole community has made her image unstable. At Randidly's company, Tatiana rejects a government land proposal designed to create leverage. Evan Crane and Senator Heathridge are connected to pressure involving a rival engineering order and an unmanaged monster threat. Randidly returns from a year of isolated training with hundreds of soul-skill riders and only weeks before another unavoidable departure. He orders rapid expansion and stockpiling and begins preparing the company to separate from government control.

Randidly turns a company festival into both a technical competition and a public statement about humanity's future. Wendy evaluates inventions, while Randidly supplies dangerous but useful engraving knowledge and studies the collective image forming around the company. Vi struggles with an image stone and the painful ritual space in her left hand. Garrett helps her but admits that an unresolved bargain drives his need to enter Randidly's order. Evan Crane's ambition to control the company becomes clear, though Randidly's projected image frightens him. In his address, Randidly explains that images can reach beyond System-granted skills and asks the company to confront its fear of inadequacy by attempting what seems impossible. The speech defines the organization's purpose, but Randidly knows that the same collective ambition could be turned toward harmful ends.

With judgment approaching, Randidly struggles to finish the city and strengthen himself. He recruits Ghost, a composite biological intelligence operating through drones, in return for a future favor. Ghost warns of several Earth-side dangers, including deaths linked to Randidly's father Ezekiel and a blood-draining killer called Stroud. Government inspectors secure mineral rights and force expensive replacements among the city's components. Nathan then examines Randidly's damaged class and finds that its earlier momentum toward level 50 has been destroyed. Using Yggdrasil, the Grim Chimera, Ignition Essence, and a strange doll-like reflection of Randidly, Nathan creates four animi and consumes them in a class-reinforcement process. The class does not truly evolve, and its lost momentum remains, but it becomes stable enough for Randidly to keep progressing while he returns to the city's final construction.

Lyra gains the Violet Moon of Yearning class and explains that Shawl's world is being pushed directly toward a fourth calamity tied to recruitment for the wider war. Her demand to be treated as an autonomous person also helps Randidly understand that a living engraving needs its own desire. He uses that insight to create growth-capable defenses for the moving city. Vi chooses to keep the painful power in her left hand and receives the Elfin Priestess dual class. Randidly then personally trains the order's applicants while Naffer prepares them for frontier defense. Senator Heathridge, financially desperate and intent on acquiring the company, arms Evan Crane with an experimental exosuit. As launch approaches, Randidly completes the city's protective engraving and gains Grim Intuition, but the new perception sharpens his fear that his pursuit of power is separating him from ordinary humanity.

Randidly accepts the violence within his Grim Chimera image without abandoning his hope for a safer world. He names the mobile city Karen and uses its reactor activation to expose Heathridge, Crane, and their infiltrators. Heathridge murders Chuck Ballard and tries to frame Randidly, but moss constructs defeat Crane's exosuit and remove the conspirators alive. Karen rises on mechanical legs and departs as an autonomous city whose spirit chooses its own path. Soon afterward, the heretic judgment arrives as a conscription order. Randidly resists but is defeated and transported to the Nether war. He awakens as a conscious Grim Chimera while his physical body lies imprisoned in a pod. Yggdrasil and Ignition of the Emerald Essence have also manifested separately. Zagnall, a dragon-headed liaison, gives the three images only days to acclimate before front-line service.

Yggdrasil reveals that he stripped Randidly-like traits from himself and Ignition Essence to preserve a coherent consciousness in the Grim Chimera, leaving the fire image disabled. Randidly volunteers to fight while Yggdrasil tends it. His first offensive mission into the Great Rift nearly erases him, but Nether Resistance unexpectedly reconnects to the imprisoned body and lets him survive. Residual Nether begins forming a defensive star in his image. Zagnall assigns him to a powerful feathered commander and promises help recovering his body if Randidly volunteers for a deadly defensive mission. The commander accepts him as her sole representative. After Zagnall pledges himself to her for the sake of his homeworld, Randidly enters Nether-controlled space under the supervision of her granite-bodied lieutenant.

Randidly survives the defensive mission by drawing ether from his imprisoned body and repeatedly repairing the Grim Chimera image. His survival attracts the feathered commander's interest, and he conceals the true body connection by crediting Yggdrasil's healing. He refuses the camp's temporary Aether Fountain blessing and instead rebuilds himself through image refinement. A turquoise-haired soldier briefly approaches him, while the commander reveals that she is a vampire-type heretic who consumes and limits subordinate images. Zagnall transfers his allegiance to her, abandoning the practical promise he made to Randidly. A corrupted image then carries a Netherwell into a neighboring camp and causes a spatial breach. Lord Milne refuses the commander's attempt to free Randidly's body, saying a superior claimant has effectively leased it. Meanwhile, the commander begins exploiting Yggdrasil's rare ability to heal damaged images.

Randidly receives two geased subordinates, one rock-bodied and one snake-headed, and assumes they may be spies. He befriends the turquoise-haired soldier after learning that the war took her brothers and estranged father and that she intends to destroy the System. On a sortie, Randidly confronts a Netherwell despite his subordinate's inability to warn him clearly. It enters his chest and tempts him with release from his fear of permanent loneliness. He rejects that promise, contains the well inside his image, and becomes able to manipulate Nether directly. He later extracts corrupting Nether from both subordinates and saves them. The turquoise-haired soldier is then assigned to a near-suicidal operation against an intelligent Gatekeeper as Randidly's connection with his main body grows strained.

Randidly joins the turquoise-haired soldier's nine-person raid team. Their mission is to locate a hidden Netherwell complex, signal the strike force, and draw its Gatekeeper toward an ambush. The soldier's destructive image carries the team through repeated attacks but consumes most of her strength. Randidly uses Nether perception to find a chamber containing hundreds of wells. She destroys most of them and collapses, while Randidly seals another well inside himself. Carrying her, he leads the surviving squad toward an ether key as the Gatekeeper pursues them. He overextends his time-based perception, cracks his identity, and falls into the Grim Chimera's instincts, but still uses the Nether veins to shift both of them to safety. The pair escapes the base, though Randidly's image and sense of self are severely damaged.

Randidly recovers from the raid while hiding his leaking Nether and growing number of stars. A front-wide bombardment confirms that the supreme commander diverted a large ether reserve, worsening the defenses. The feathered commander considers Randidly a political asset and renews efforts to gain his body, while Zagnall returns as her spy. Randidly develops a rotating-core weapon and discovers that Nether rituals resemble the foundations of Nexus classes. A deep-raiding investigator arrives with the surviving turquoise-haired soldier, seeking proof that an image can form stars. The supreme commander then assigns Randidly a strategically important ether-key mission that appears designed to kill him. The commander is personally hostile because of losses tied to Randidly's judgment, and his remarks suggest a plan involving Randidly's body and world. As compensation, Randidly is allowed to choose two Fates from a guarded armory.

At the fate armory, Randidly endures the tests of two elders whose dead daughter's fire Fate persists as a dormant sword blade. Nadia openly hopes the Fate will consume him and restore her daughter, but Randidly chooses it as a possible weapon against the supreme commander's scheme. Rather than submit, he awakens the blade with ether and confines it inside his own internal world using Nether. He leaves burned but alive, also carrying a wooden trunk sealed by an extraordinary ivory lock. Nadia gives the rock-bodied subordinate an unexplained future gift, while the other elder incapacitates the now dragon-like subordinate after a provocation. Randidly, Salazar, and the two subordinates then enter the Great Rift with the strategic key. There, Randidly forms its protective image into an ether-powered shelter modeled on a small house and farm.

Randidly deliberately drains the strategic key while training, learning the blade Fate, and corroding the trunk's lock. Four false Nether cores shatter and condense into his first true core. Through Nether rituals he watches the turquoise-haired soldier reject pressure to join an elite brigade, then accept its training while trying not to become only a weapon of destruction. He also sees Alana return to Mount Olympus after weeks of solitary hunting. She defines herself as a hunter rather than the embodiment of her city, ambushes the Ice Dragon Broodmother, and gains new abilities. Instead of killing the injured dragon, Alana names Randidly as someone willing to oppose the Nexus and begins a conversation about him. The dragon attacks cease, but no alliance is confirmed. Meanwhile, the ivory lock corrodes far faster than Randidly can explain.

Earth's zones gather for their first World Summit. They agree to cooperate against the remaining epic-dungeon disasters, but Zone 1 displays Mjolnir, a long-range weapon that establishes a coercive advantage over the other delegates. Randidly fears its construction may involve human souls. He reaches Vi through a Nether ritual and uses her as an intermediary to restore his order's weakening image stones, leaving a stronger Grim Chimera presence in their training. He watches Yggdrasil exhaust himself healing the front and offer eventual surrender in exchange for support for the feathered commander's larger project. Tatiana continues running Karen and receives Felicia, a borderlands refugee and former partner who questions Randidly's absence. Randidly eventually forms a second true Nether core. His remote observation of the bloodless Zone 19 murders leads him to identify his father Ezekiel as the probable killer.

Ezekiel and Ace attempt to seize a healer in Zone 19 but are surrounded by blood beasts controlled by Stroud. Ace's Dauntless image is defeated and he is badly injured, though Ezekiel teleports the group away. Randidly opens the ancient trunk and finds an inert fingerless glove, then discovers that Ignition Essence's cracked containment is close to failure. Earth prepares for an Ogre Gorge assault with a specialized shield forged by Sam. Theodora Grayman becomes the World Summit's first chairwoman, while the bloodless murders pause and the Rakshasi remains a threat. At the front, the turquoise-haired soldier learns that her father died fighting Gatekeepers and resolves to protect others without denying human vulnerability. Randidly discovers that Nether's Caress may open an escape portal. Almost immediately, the strategic key fails, allowing a Nether King and a vast army with many Gatekeeper-level forces to advance on the outnumbered defenders.

The front-line commanders argue over a captured Nether Prince as the invasion reaches their defenses. The turquoise-haired soldier rejects their priorities and confronts a six-tailed Gatekeeper, wounding it before a strike through her shoulder leaves her unable to continue. The supreme commander declares the Grim Chimera dead and attempts to claim Randidly's remaining images, but the suppression pod is found empty. Randidly has used Nether's Caress to move his physical body through the Great Rift and reunite it with the Grim Chimera. Disguised within the Nether army, he reaches the wounded soldier and reveals himself. Yggdrasil then reunites with him, and the evolved Absolute Grasp of Yggdrasil destroys most of a ten-thousand-beast force. The feathered commander and her lieutenant move against the remaining elites. Randidly's body, ether, five Nether cores, and Yggdrasil are united, but Ignition Essence remains missing, the soldier is badly wounded, and Gatekeeper-level enemies keep the battle unresolved.

characters.description: An orphan of Camorr's plague years, sold as a small boy by the master of a thieves' orphanage to a blind beggar-priest who saw what he could become. He now leads the Gentlemen Bastards, a crew that passes for a modest gang of cutpurses while quietly robbing the city's nobility for enormous sums. Slight, unremarkable to look at and no kind of fighter, he works through preparation, nerve and improvisation, wearing invented identities for months at a time and enjoying the performance more than the money, which the crew never spends. He answers to Camorr's crime lord like every other thief in the city, and breaks that man's single most important rule as a matter of daily business.
characters.name: Locke Lamora

characters.description: Locke's closest friend and the crew's muscle. The orphaned son of prosperous Camorri merchants, he was raised to keep ledgers before a fire took his parents, and he has kept both trades: he manages the Gentlemen Bastards' accounts, reads for pleasure, and was trained in close fighting by one of the city's finest swordmasters. Heavyset, bespectacled and mild in company, he carries a matched pair of hatchets he calls the Wicked Sisters. In the crew's current game he plays the silent northern bodyguard of a foreign merchant.
characters.name: Jean Tannen

characters.description: One of the Sanza twins, raised alongside Locke and Jean beneath the temple. He and his brother are near identical, trade on the confusion constantly, and handle the forgery, sleight of hand and quick-change work that a game needs when one man has to be in two places. Mocking, restless company, and a capable cook when his turn at the kitchen comes round.
characters.name: Calo Sanza

characters.description: The other Sanza twin and Calo's inseparable partner in the Gentlemen Bastards' work. The pair are interchangeable to almost everyone, including on occasion their own crew, and they use it deliberately: two men who can pass for one open up tricks nobody else in Camorr can run. Like his brother he is quick, irreverent, and a better cook than any thief needs to be.
characters.name: Galdo Sanza

characters.description: The crew's apprentice, an orphan of about twelve taken out of the same thieves' orphanage that produced Locke. He does the climbing, watching and running that the games require, is desperate to be counted a full member, and is repeatedly told that the fastest way to lose the place he wants is to improvise without being asked.
characters.name: Bug

characters.description: The blind beggar-priest of the god of mercy who bought Locke from the Thiefmaker and raised him, Jean, the Sanzas and the others in the vault beneath his temple. Both his blindness and his order are a long fraud: he serves the unnamed god of thieves, and his real work is training children in languages, etiquette, cookery, accounting and the confidence trade until they can sit at a noble's table without being noticed. He appears in the chapters that look back at the crew's upbringing, and his lessons underlie everything Locke does.
characters.name: Father Chains

characters.description: A former scholar from the north who took Camorr's underworld by force and has held it for more than twenty years from a moored galleon called the Floating Grave. Every gang in the city pays him tribute. His rule rests on the Secret Peace, a private arrangement with the duke's people under which thieves may prey on the common folk as they like and must never touch the nobility, and he enforces it without exception, which makes the Gentlemen Bastards' actual trade a killing offence. He has grown heavier and grimmer since his wife's death, and surrounds himself with his grown children and his bodyguards.
characters.name: Capa Vencarlo Barsavi

characters.description: A young Camorri nobleman with a taste for speculative ventures and very little experience of being lied to. Recently married and keen to build a fortune of his own rather than live on his family's, he is the mark of the crew's current game: a chance to buy into a northern brandy house, offered to him by a foreign merchant he believes he saved from a mugging.
characters.name: Don Lorenzo Salvara

characters.description: Don Lorenzo's wife, an alchemical botanist trained at the Therin Collegium whose greenhouse work is the real source of the family's money. She is sharper and far more sceptical than her husband, checks what she is told, and is the single hardest part of keeping the Salvara game upright.
characters.name: Dona Sofia Salvara

characters.description: Master of the Shades' Hill orphanage, who takes in Camorr's unwanted and plague-orphaned children and trains them to steal for him. He sells Locke on because the boy's ambitions have already cost lives and threaten to draw exactly the kind of attention a gang of child thieves cannot survive.
characters.name: The Thiefmaker

characters.description: Capa Barsavi's only daughter and, since her brothers are blunter instruments, the most capable of his children. She has known Locke since they were both children in the same gang and treats him with rough affection. Her father intends her to inherit his position, and has settled views about whom she ought to marry in order to hold it.
characters.name: Nazca Barsavi

characters.description: Twin sisters who serve as Capa Barsavi's personal bodyguards and are the most celebrated shark-fighters in Camorr, drawing crowds at the floating carnival where they kill in the water for the city's entertainment. Silent, identical and universally feared, they wear trophies taken from their kills.
characters.name: Cheryn and Raiza Berangias

characters.description: A figure nobody has seen clearly who has begun killing Capa Barsavi's gang leaders one at a time, leaving no witnesses and no explanation. He appears to want the capa's chair, and to command resources no Camorri criminal should be able to afford. Barsavi's people cannot find him, and the killings are steadily emptying the capa's court while the city's thieves take sides in advance.
characters.name: The Grey King

characters.description: A Bondsmage of Karthain, one of the mercenary sorcerers whose guild is feared across the continent and priced accordingly. He is accompanied everywhere by a scorpion hawk called Vestris, through whose eyes he can see. The Bondsmagi are protected by one rule that everybody obeys: harm a single member and the entire guild answers, so no one in Camorr will lift a hand against him whatever he does while under contract.
characters.name: The Falconer

characters.description: A Gentleman Bastard raised with Locke, Jean and the Sanzas under Father Chains, and the only girl among them. By Locke's account she is better than he is at every part of the work. She has not been in Camorr for years, and Locke, who has loved her since they were children, is unable to discuss her sensibly with anyone.
characters.name: Sabetha Belacoros

characters.description: The elderly Countess Amberglass, long widowed and childless, who presides over the noblewomen's gatherings in her glass tower and spends most of them apparently dozing over her knitting while her guests talk around her. Camorri society treats her as a harmless fixture and speaks freely in front of her.
characters.name: Dona Angiavesta Vorchenza

recaps.ending: Locke kills Capa Raza aboard the Floating Grave and survives the fight only just, with Jean carrying him out. Raza's revenge on Barsavi is complete but his second scheme fails: the attack he prepared for Camorr's assembled nobility at the duke's feast is stopped because Locke gave the warning to the Spider in time. That officer turns out to be Dona Vorchenza, the elderly countess nobody took seriously. She knows exactly who Locke is and cannot prove any of it, and she lets him go rather than pursue him. The Falconer is collected by his own guild, mutilated and out of his mind; the Bondsmagi make it plain that what was done to him will be answered in their own time and on their own schedule, so Locke and Jean leave Camorr with an enemy that outlasts the city. Calo, Galdo, Bug and Nazca Barsavi are dead, the Gentlemen Bastards' hoarded fortune is scattered, and the temple that hid them is finished as a home. Locke and Jean take ship out of Camorr as the last two of the crew Chains raised, with their skills, each other, and very little else.
recaps.in_short: In the canal city of Camorr, thieves live under the Secret Peace: they may rob the common folk as they please and must never touch the nobility. Locke Lamora, raised by a fraudulent blind priest to be a confidence artist rather than a cutpurse, breaks that rule for a living, running elaborate swindles on the aristocracy with his small crew, the Gentlemen Bastards. While he works his latest mark, a masked figure called the Grey King begins murdering the crime lord Capa Barsavi's captains, and a hired sorcerer of the Bondsmagi forces Locke to serve the Grey King's scheme. The trap closes: Barsavi is destroyed, the Grey King takes the city's underworld as Capa Raza, and three of the Gentlemen Bastards are murdered along with the crew's fortune. Locke and Jean Tannen, the only survivors, take the sorcerer apart, expose Raza's plan to slaughter Camorr's nobility to the duke's secret intelligence chief, and Locke kills Raza himself. They leave the city avenged, ruined, and permanently marked by the sorcerers' guild.

recaps.text: Camorr is a canal city built on the indestructible glass ruins of a vanished people, ruled by a duke and his nobility above and by Capa Vencarlo Barsavi's gangs below. The two halves are joined by the Secret Peace: the underworld may rob the common folk freely so long as it never touches an aristocrat, and the watch leaves it alone in return. Locke Lamora, sold as a child to the fraudulent blind priest Father Chains and raised in the vault beneath his temple, now leads the Gentlemen Bastards - Jean Tannen, the twins Calo and Galdo Sanza, and the boy Bug. To Barsavi they are a small gang of unambitious thieves paying their tribute. In fact they break the Secret Peace as a profession, running long confidence games on the nobility and hoarding the proceeds unspent in a vault under the temple. Their current mark is Don Lorenzo Salvara, whom Locke, disguised as a northern brandy merchant, persuades to invest heavily in a venture that does not exist, and whose sharper wife Sofia has to be handled as carefully as the don himself. Interleaved chapters show the crew's childhood and Chains teaching them the trade.

Barsavi's court is in trouble. Someone calling himself the Grey King has begun murdering the capa's gang leaders one at a time, without witnesses, and Barsavi has withdrawn to his moored galleon refusing to move against an enemy he cannot find. Summoned by the capa's daughter Nazca, an old friend of Locke's from their orphanage days, Locke learns that Barsavi means her to inherit and means Locke to marry her in order to steady the succession. The Salvara game continues to pay well. Then the Grey King reaches for Locke directly: he is taken by a Bondsmage of Karthain called the Falconer, a hired sorcerer whose guild nobody dares harm, and delivered to the Grey King, who orders Locke to impersonate him at a parley with Barsavi. Refusal is not on offer: the Bondsmage's presence removes every option that involves force, and the errand will put Locke in a room between the two most dangerous men in Camorr.

The Grey King's grip tightens. Nazca Barsavi, going to negotiate on her father's behalf, is murdered and her body returned to the capa, which removes any prospect of a settlement. Locke keeps the Salvara game running while preparing to stand in front of Barsavi wearing another man's name, and Jean, the only person who knows the whole shape of it, can find no way out. At the Echo Hole, Locke goes through with the impersonation and Barsavi springs the ambush he has spent days preparing. It is Barsavi who has been played. His own bodyguards, the Berangias sisters, turn on him, his sons are killed, and the Grey King reveals himself and has the capa drowned in the same cask his daughter's body came back in. The Grey King takes Camorr's underworld for himself under the name Capa Raza. Locke is stabbed, sealed in a barrel and thrown into the bay. Jean pulls him out alive. They return to the temple and find Calo, Galdo and Bug murdered in the vault below it and the crew's entire fortune gone.

Locke, badly wounded and half destroyed by grief, is kept alive largely by Jean's stubbornness while Camorr's gangs swear to their new capa. Raza consolidates fast, buying loyalty with the money he took from the Gentlemen Bastards and dispensing favours from Barsavi's old galleon, and the city adjusts to him within days. Locke refuses to leave while the man is alive, which reduces the two of them to a plan with no crew, no money and no protection behind it. At the same time the other danger the Salvara con has stirred up comes closer: the duke's secret intelligence service, run by an officer known only as the Spider, has been hunting the thief the nobility call the Thorn of Camorr, and the trail of the brandy swindle leads to him. Locke begins improvising a way to reach a man guarded by an entire underworld and by a Bondsmage.

Locke and Jean go after Raza with the only tools they have left. Locke works his way back into the city's business under a string of borrowed identities while Jean deals with the more direct obstacles: confronting the Berangias sisters, he kills them both. The pair then take the Falconer, whose protection proves less absolute than he believed. They kill his scorpion hawk, which unhinges him, and then cut out his tongue and take his fingers so that he can never work sorcery again, leaving his guild a living man to collect and a message they will not forget. Raza's motive is now clear: he is the surviving son of a merchant family destroyed years earlier by Barsavi with the duke's tacit consent, the Berangias sisters were his sisters, and every killing since has been payment against that debt. It is equally clear that he does not intend to stop with Barsavi, and that Camorr's nobility are the rest of the account.

Raza's remaining plan is aimed at the aristocracy, who will all be gathered in one place for the duke's feast in the sky-tower of Raven's Reach. Locke, caught by the duke's secret service before he can move, discovers that the Spider is Dona Vorchenza, the elderly countess the whole city has been dismissing for decades. He trades what he knows for the freedom to act; the warning reaches her in time and the nobility survive the attack Raza had prepared for them. Locke then goes after Raza in person. Aboard the Floating Grave he kills him, at very nearly the cost of his own life, and Jean gets him out. Calo, Galdo, Bug and Nazca are avenged, the crew's hoarded fortune is scattered beyond recovery, and Locke and Jean are the only two left of the family Chains built.

characters.description: A failed wizard of Ankh-Morpork's Unseen University, expelled after one of the eight great spells of the Octavo lodged itself in his mind and crowded out everything he tried to learn afterwards. He can cast nothing, speaks several languages, and treats running away as a skill worth being good at. Since being pressed into service as guide to the Disc's first tourist he has been carried from one disaster to the next, and the book opens with him falling off the edge of the world. His hat is embroidered with the word wizzard.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A small, cheerful insurance clerk from the wealthy Agatean Empire on the far side of the Disc, and the first tourist the Discworld has ever had. He carries a picture-making box, a phrasebook, and an unshakeable belief that the world is fundamentally a friendly place put on for his benefit. He does not recognise danger when it is directly in front of him, which has so far worked out better for him than it has for anyone travelling with him.
characters.name: Twoflower

characters.description: Twoflower's travelling chest, made of sapient pearwood and moving on hundreds of small legs. It holds far more than its size allows, follows its owner across continents and through impossible places, and destroys anything that threatens him. It cannot be reasoned with, outrun, or left behind.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: The vast star turtle on whose shell four elephants stand carrying the Discworld. Astronomers on the Disc have noticed that it has changed course and is swimming steadily toward a red star that grows larger in the sky with every passing day, and nobody knows why.
characters.name: Great A'Tuin

characters.description: The anthropomorphic personification of death, a robed skeleton with a scythe who speaks in a voice that arrives directly inside the listener's head. He collects the souls of the notable and the interesting, keeps a careful diary of appointments, and has been trying to keep an appointment with Rincewind for some time without success. He is patient, literal-minded, and increasingly curious about the living.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: The Archchancellor of Unseen University and the most senior wizard on the Disc, weighed down with ceremonial titles and a robe to match. Elderly, imperious, and thoroughly conventional, he treats magic as a matter of ritual and precedence. When the Octavo begins acting on its own he takes charge of the University's response and attempts to recover the missing spell by force of high magic.
characters.name: Galder Weatherwax

characters.description: A young senior wizard of Unseen University, unusual among his colleagues for being neither fat nor obviously magical. He keeps files, draws up organisational charts, and thinks of the University as an institution to be managed rather than a brotherhood of spellcasters. He is patient, tidy, and quietly determined to climb every rung of the eight orders of wizardry, and he pays close attention to what the Octavo is doing.
characters.name: Ymper Trymon

characters.description: A mercenary captain hired to bring Rincewind back to Unseen University alive. Competent, practical, and impatient with the men she leads, she is a professional in a trade that mostly attracts amateurs, and she pursues her quarry across country with more persistence than her employers expected.
characters.name: Herrena the Henna-Haired Harridan

characters.description: The Disc's greatest hero, now eighty-seven years old, toothless, thin as a stick, and still alive after a career that has killed every rival he ever had. He has been robbing temples and fighting monsters since before most kingdoms existed, owns almost nothing, and has strong opinions about the modern habit of wearing trousers. Age has cost him his teeth and much of his hearing but none of his speed or nerve.
characters.name: Cohen the Barbarian

characters.description: A young woman of the Circle Sea country who was chosen by her people's druids as a sacrifice at a stone circle, and who is unimpressed by the honour. Sensible, blunt, and quick to organise the people around her, she attaches herself to the travellers after being freed and takes a particular interest in Cohen.
characters.name: Bethan

characters.description: The keeper of Unseen University's library, the largest collection of magical books on the Disc. A surge of raw magic turns him into an orangutan, and once he discovers how convenient long arms are for reaching high shelves he declines every offer to be turned back. He communicates in a single syllable, is enormously strong, and is fiercely protective of the books in his care.
characters.name: The Librarian

characters.description: The Discworld's most powerful book of magic, written by the Creator and holding the eight great spells that underpin the world. It sits chained in a cellar beneath Unseen University, is aware of its own contents, and has begun taking an interest in the fact that one of its spells is missing.
characters.name: The Octavo

recaps.ending: Trymon takes the Octavo, reads seven of the eight great spells directly into his mind, and is immediately hollowed out and worn by the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions, which use him as a doorway into the world. Rincewind climbs the Tower of Art and confronts him, and after being pursued through a landscape inside Trymon's head he destroys him with a half-brick in a sock. With the Things beaten back, Rincewind reads the Octavo, the eighth spell finally leaving his mind, and the eight spells together settle the world. The red star turns out not to be a threat at all: Great A'Tuin was swimming to it to give birth, and eight small turtles hatch and swim away from the star carrying eight tiny worlds of their own, with the Disc passing safely by. Rincewind, at last free of the spell, can begin learning ordinary magic and returns to Unseen University as a student. Twoflower decides he has seen enough of the world and goes home to the Agatean Empire, leaving the Luggage behind as a parting gift to Rincewind, who is now stuck with it. Cohen the Barbarian and Bethan are married, and Cohen settles into a comfortable position in the Circle Sea kingdoms.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind and Twoflower fall off the edge of the Discworld and are saved when the great spell lodged in Rincewind's head rewrites reality to put them back on it, because it has work for him. A red star is growing in the Disc's sky and Great A'Tuin is swimming straight at it; the wizards of Unseen University learn that the eight spells of the Octavo must be read together to save the world, and one of them is inside Rincewind. Hunted by mercenaries hired by the ambitious wizard Trymon, the pair cross the continent with the aging hero Cohen the Barbarian and a rescued sacrifice named Bethan, while Trymon murders the Archchancellor and seizes control of the University. In Ankh-Morpork, with the star filling the sky and the city in the grip of panic and star cults, Trymon reads the Octavo himself and is possessed by creatures from the Dungeon Dimensions. Rincewind kills him at the top of the Tower of Art and reads the spells, and the star proves to be where Great A'Tuin was going to hatch eight baby turtles. Freed of his spell at last, Rincewind returns to the University, and Twoflower goes home, leaving him the Luggage.

recaps.text: Previously: Rincewind, an inept wizard expelled from Unseen University after one of the eight great spells of the Octavo lodged itself in his mind, was ordered by the Patrician of Ankh-Morpork to act as guide to Twoflower, the Discworld's first tourist, a rich and relentlessly optimistic insurance clerk from the distant Agatean Empire. Twoflower's introduction of insurance burned much of Ankh-Morpork to the ground, and the two fled the city together, accompanied by Twoflower's Luggage, a walking chest of sapient pearwood that is devoted to its owner and lethal to everyone else. Their travels took them through a temple of the ancient evil Bel-Shamharoth and the dragon-haunted Wyrmberg to the kingdom of Krull at the very Rim of the world, where scholars intended to sacrifice them to a voyage over the edge. They escaped, only to be swept over the Rimfall themselves, and the story broke off with the pair falling off the edge of the Discworld into open space.

As Rincewind and Twoflower fall off the Disc, reality shifts around them and they find themselves alive in a forest, deposited back on the world. The cause is the spell in Rincewind's head, one of the eight great spells of the Octavo, which has decided it needs him alive. At Unseen University the Octavo, the Creator's own book of magic, has begun acting without being asked; the wizards discover that the world is in danger and that all eight spells must be spoken together to save it. Above the Disc a red star has appeared and is growing, and Great A'Tuin, the turtle carrying the world, is swimming directly toward it. The Archchancellor, Galder Weatherwax, sets out to recover the missing spell by summoning Rincewind back to the University, watched closely by Ymper Trymon, an ambitious young wizard with a filing system and plans of his own. Death, meanwhile, continues to turn up wherever Rincewind is, and continues to be disappointed.

Galder's summoning fails to fetch Rincewind, so the University's response becomes less refined: a band of mercenaries under Herrena the Henna-Haired Harridan is hired to bring the wizard in alive. Rincewind and Twoflower keep moving through the countryside with Herrena's people behind them, at one point taking shelter in a shop that appears in places where no shop was and vanishes again afterwards, its owner condemned to wander between worlds. Across the Disc the red star grows brighter and ordinary people begin to notice it, and the wizards' assurances that everything is under control convince nobody. Panic follows: mobs form in the cities, wizards are blamed for whatever the star turns out to be, and cults spring up devoted to welcoming it.

Still pursued, Rincewind and Twoflower fall in with Cohen the Barbarian, the Disc's greatest hero, now eighty-seven, toothless and entirely undiminished in every other respect. Together they interrupt a druid ceremony at a stone circle, where a young woman named Bethan has been selected as a sacrifice, and get her away from the priests. Bethan joins the party and quickly makes herself indispensable, and she and Cohen take a clear liking to each other. At Unseen University, Galder Weatherwax dies in a magical accident that Trymon arranges and then presents as a tragedy, which leaves Trymon in charge of the University and of the search for the eighth spell. The raw magic now loose in the world also turns the Librarian into an orangutan; discovering that this makes shelving considerably easier, he refuses to be changed back. The star continues to swell in the sky, and magic itself begins to behave unreliably as the world approaches it.
